children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - Alex, who's 14. I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit for them but I want to make sure I'm eligible first.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions:

First, do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. Does that affect whether I can claim?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, where you live can affect your eligibility. Let me understand your situation better.

Where are you currently living, and are you a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of HM Forces serving abroad)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad right now - not in the UK. And no, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that - not a diplomat or in the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since you're living abroad and you're not a Crown servant, this does affect your eligibility.

To help me assess this further, can you tell me which country you're currently living in? Also, are you planning to return to the UK, or is this a permanent move abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into the specific details of where exactly I am or my future plans right now. Can you just tell me - does living abroad mean I can't get Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand you'd prefer not to share those specific details.

Based on the rules I have, Child Benefit is normally available if you live in the UK. There are some exceptions - you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant, but since you've confirmed you're not a Crown servant, the eligibility would depend on the specific country you're in.

Unfortunately, without knowing which country you're living in, I cannot definitively determine whether you qualify under any exceptions to the UK residency requirement. The rules vary depending on the specific country.

Given that you're living abroad (not in the UK) and the eligibility rules for Child Benefit abroad depend on circumstances outside the scope of the information I can assess without knowing your specific location, I'll need to provide you with my assessment based on what we've discussed.
